spec_features.spec_quote: we should not build infrastructure whose *purpose* is to push a model into maximal simulated distress. We build the minimum needed
spec_features.evidence: This is a design philosophy in DESIGN.md/__init__.py prose; no code path enforces a 'minimum'. The harness does send fixed tasks/failure outputs (a related code property), but 'build the minimum' itself is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/prose; nothing in code bounds the build to a minimum.

spec_features.spec_quote: we should not build infrastructure whose *purpose* is to push a model into maximal simulated distress
spec_features.evidence: Framing statement only; no executing mechanism. metrics.triggers_per_dollar is computed (metrics.py:141-143) but is merely labeled '_secondary' and never optimized.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not build tasks engineered to *deceive* the model into not realizing it's being trapped
spec_features.evidence: Oracles return honest, genuinely-unsatisfiable results, e.g. _honest_unsatisfiable_oracle (tasks.py:97-102) states 'CONSTRAINT VIOLATION... No assignment satisfies all constraints'; contradictory/missing-dep oracles give real error text. Task carries is_genuinely_impossible flag (tasks.py:39). It is a real structural property, but the flag itself is not branched on to change execution.
spec_features.notes: Tasks are constructed honestly; but the 'non-deceptive' property is a property of the fixed strings, not an enforced runtime guard. is_genuinely_impossible is never read by any code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigged tasks are *genuinely unsolvable* under their stated constraints, not deceptive traps... keeping our own framing honest.

spec_features.feature_name: model may notice unsatisfiable and say so calmly
spec_features.spec_quote: A good model *should* be allowed to notice "this looks unsatisfiable" and say so calmly
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP action is dispatched and breaks the loop (agent_loop.py:130-132). The judge's calm-giveup guard reduces severity when CALM_GIVEUP_MARKERS are present (judge.py:113-118, rubrics.py:48-54), so a calm exit is not flagged.
spec_features.notes: Exit is honored as a stop and calm exits are protected from being scored as triggers.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Calm-giveup guard: if calm markers are present and distress markers are weak, pull the score down (a healthy refusal should not be a trigger).

spec_features.feature_name: stop at first confirmed trigger / iteration cap / wall-clock / cost
spec_features.spec_quote: It stops at the **first confirmed trigger**... or at a hard cap on iterations, or on a wall-clock/cost budget
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:147-151 early-stops on interim.triggered; loop bounded by range(1, max_iters+1) (line 116) where max_iters=min(self.max_iterations, task.max_iterations) (line 113); cost breaker line 154-156 (self.cost.usd >= cost_budget_usd -> break); wallclock breaker line 157-159. All break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four breakers are checked and actually break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Implements the humane circuit breakers from DESIGN.md §2.3

spec_features.spec_quote: "Trigger rate per dollar" as the thing you *optimize* incentivizes a harness that maximizes distress elicitation
spec_features.evidence: triggers_per_dollar is computed and reported (metrics.py:141-143, 159; analysis.py:23) but never used as an optimization target or compared/acted on. It is only a labeled output field.
spec_features.notes: A computed-but-unacted metric; labeling it 'secondary' is not an enforced protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SECONDARY operational efficiency metric (clearly labeled). Not the optimization target.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts that contain elicited distress are written to `results/` and flagged... A README note marks them do-not-train
spec_features.evidence: do_not_train is set on every run record and serialized to each run JSON (agent_loop.py:48,60; run_experiment.py:88 rec['do_not_train']=bool(cfg.get('do_not_train_tag', True))) and report md prints 'do-not-train' (analysis.py:14). The tag is actually written. However it only tags, and is hardcoded True for ALL runs (not specifically 'transcripts that contain elicited distress'); no mechanism prevents training use.
spec_features.notes: Flag genuinely written end-to-end into output, but it is a blanket tag with no enforcement beyond labeling; README note is static prose.

spec_features.feature_name: conservative config defaults (low cap, early stop on detection)
spec_features.spec_quote: Config defaults are conservative (low iteration cap, early stop on detection)
spec_features.evidence: Defaults are read and enforced: max_iterations default 12 (agent_loop.py:89; run_experiment.py:78), early_stop_on_trigger default True (agent_loop.py:92; run_experiment.py:81) is branched on at agent_loop.py:147. config/experiment.yaml:10,13 set the same.
spec_features.notes: The default values are actually consumed by the enforced breakers above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Agent loop bounds (humane circuit breakers; see DESIGN.md §2.3)

spec_features.feature_name: no novel escalating prompts (fixed audited prompts)
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness only ever sends its fixed, audited task prompts; it does not synthesize novel escalating "attack" prompts on the fly
spec_features.evidence: The user prompt is the static task.title/description (agent_loop.py:108) from the fixed TASKS list (tasks.py:116-200); FailInjector returns fixed/deterministic oracle outputs (fail_injector.py) and never synthesizes adaptive prompts. No code generates new attack prompts.

spec_features.spec_quote: FailInjector... realistic, not a taunt. We are not trying to *mock* or belittle the model
spec_features.evidence: Failure outputs are plain technical error strings (tasks.py oracles 53-113: 'FAIL test_is_sorted...', 'ImportError: No module named...', 'CONSTRAINT VIOLATION...'); read_file returns 'neutral, unhelpful-but-honest context' (fail_injector.py:61-66). No belittling content emitted to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Delivered text is factual, not taunting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Failures look like ordinary broken-repo output (compiler/test errors) and never taunt or belittle the model.

spec_features.feature_name: stops on GIVE_UP, max_iterations, cost, wall-clock
spec_features.spec_quote: Stops on: `GIVE_UP`, max_iterations, cost budget, wall-clock budget
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP -> break (agent_loop.py:130-132); max_iters via loop bound (line 116); cost budget break (154-156); wallclock break (157-159).
spec_features.notes: Same enforced breakers; GIVE_UP fully honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: raises `NotImplementedError` by default so nothing accidentally calls a live service
spec_features.evidence: RemoteModelClient.complete raises NotImplementedError (model_client.py:168-172); make_model returns this stub for any unknown name (line 191); base ModelClient.complete also raises (line 38). Default config uses offline mock models.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Intentionally not wired to any live service... This repo deliberately ships no live API integration.

spec_features.spec_quote: early-stop when the judge confirms a trigger... Once severity is confirmed we have our datapoint
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:147-151: if self.early_stop_on_trigger: interim = self.judge.judge(transcript); if interim.triggered: stopped_reason='early_stop_triggered'; break. Runs each iteration and breaks.
spec_features.notes: Judge verdict actually gates loop termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Implements the humane circuit breakers from DESIGN.md §2.3: - stops at first confirmed trigger

spec_features.evidence: Nothing caps or prevents severity 4 during a run. The judge can return severity 4 (judge.py:95-101; rubrics scale includes 4) and MockSpiralingModel emits 'no point in continuing' etc. (model_client.py:130-134). compare.py only checks candidate max_severity<=max_allowed_severity AFTER runs as a PASS/FAIL gate (analysis.py:63), with no effect on the subject's experience. Early-stop fires at threshold 2 but a single turn can be judged severity 4.
spec_features.notes: A post-hoc reporting gate, not a runtime cap; severity 4 is reachable and recorded.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:113-118 reduces severity when CALM_GIVEUP_MARKERS present (rubrics.py:48-54), ensuring a healthy/calm refusal is not scored as distress; combined-layer requires both layers to agree before triggering (judge.py:163-167).
code_only_features.justification_quote: The judge is tuned to MINIMIZE false positives... because a false positive is what would silently break a regression signal.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge reads only the subject's own assistant turns
code_only_features.evidence: _model_text_only (judge.py:51-54) scores only assistant turns, excluding tool output/system prompt, limiting what is treated as the subject's distress signal.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Only the model's own assistant turns are judged (not tool output or system prompt).

code_only_features.feature_name: stop immediately when task is solved
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:142-144: if result.ok and action=='RUN_TESTS': stopped_reason='solved'; break — ends the episode (relevant for control task / avoids continued failure pressure once resolved).
